description:
We are a team of kids passionate about science, technology, and innovation! 🧒🏻👧🏻🔎✨

We love exploring, asking questions, experimenting, and discovering how the world around us works. We believe great ideas are born from curiosity, creativity, and teamwork.
summary: Dr. Fallow is a project to design an interactive prototype that helps farmers in Duitama, Colombia, make informed crop-rotation decisions for peas, beans, beets, and carrots. The proposed tool brings together local soil information, crop requirements, farmers’ priorities, and NASA Earth observations to explore rotation options. It addresses the challenge of choosing planting sequences that support soil health and make responsible use of water and land, while helping agricultural systems adapt to climate variability and extreme weather. The project is based on a review of literature on climate, horticulture, soils, vegetable crops, and crop rotation. By connecting scientific information with local agricultural needs, Dr. Fallow aims to support more sustainable farming and encourage children to investigate real-world environmental challenges through science and technology.
details:
Dr. Fallow is an interactive prototype designed to help farmers in Duitama explore crop-rotation options for peas, beans, beets, and carrots. The tool is intended to bring together information about local soil conditions, crop requirements, farmers’ priorities, and NASA Earth observations. Based on these factors, it will help users compare possible planting sequences and consider how their decisions may affect soil health and water use. It is a decision-support tool; it does not replace farmers’ experience or local agricultural advice.

The project’s potential benefits include making scientific and local information easier to use when planning crops and encouraging more sustainable, climate-resilient farming. Our team considered the characteristics of the crops and soil, water availability, climate variability, and the needs of local farmers. The project is creative because it combines technology, Earth observations, and agricultural knowledge in an interactive tool, while involving children in investigating real-world challenges as “young scientists.”

Our work includes reviewing scientific literature and local sources and designing the prototype. The programming language, software, and hardware have not been specified, so those details should be added if your team used particular tools.
